title: kv-prefetch-vs-prefetchless-trace-nsight-compare-2029-09
content:
Purpose:
Compare two KV cache strategies under inference load: (A) aggressive prefetching of KV pages into GPU memory before token decode vs (B) on-demand (prefetchless) fetch during decode. Goal is to identify why prefetching sometimes increases tail latency and reduces effective SM occupancy despite reducing copy stalls in microbenchmarks.

High-level hypothesis:
- Prefetching reduces host->device copy stalls but can create synchronized kernel launch bursts and raise stream contention (especially when combined with CUDA graphs), causing SM scheduling inefficiencies and lower warp execution efficiency.
- Prefetchless approach has more small DMA events but spreads kernel launches more evenly, which can keep SMs busier and reduce tail latency under heterogeneous request patterns.

What I captured:
- Two Nsight sessions (session ids embedded in filenames below) run back-to-back on same Dedicated node (A100s, PCIe gen4):
  - nsight_session_kv_prefetch_2029-09-15.rdc (prefetch strategy A)
  - nsight_session_kv_on_demand_2029-09-16.rdc (strategy B)
- Workload: synthetic chat pipeline, token-by-token decode, 4 concurrent workers sending 1 request/sec, avg sequence length 180, 8 warmup tokens pinned.
- Runtime build: inference-runtime v3.8.1 (opt-kernel-set v17), CUDA 12.3, cuBLAS/PRIM versions as in GH commit above.

Key metrics (aggregated from Nsight and runtime telemetry):
- Prefetch (A):
  - mean per-token latency: ~9.7ms
  - tail 95/99: 22ms / 58ms
  - average SM achieved_occupancy: 64%
  - average SM active_warps per SM: 18 (on A100 SM cap 32)
  - warp_execution_efficiency: 73%
  - observed kernel-launch bursts: spikes of 1800 launches/sec during prefetch flush (nsight timeline)
  - DMA pattern: two large host->device batches of 2.6GB each per request (depends on kv set)
- Prefetchless (B):
  - mean per-token latency: ~10.2ms
  - tail 95/99: 16ms / 29ms
  - average SM achieved_occupancy: 72%
  - average SM active_warps per SM: 22
  - warp_execution_efficiency: 84%
  - kernel launches: steady ~650 launches/sec, more interleaving across streams
  - DMA pattern: many small host->device transfers (hundreds of 8–64KB transfers per request) but overlapped better with kernel work

Observations from Nsight traces and timeline analysis:
1) Launch bursts and stream serialization: Prefetching funnels large amounts of work onto the high-priority stream (the prefetch callback path), which then submits many small kernels in tight succession once the prefetch completes. Nsight shows tight clusters of kernel launches separated by brief idle gaps where SMs are waiting on next kernel to be queued. This creates a sawtooth utilization rather than a smooth plateau.
2) Kernel size & occupancy mismatch: Many prefetched kernels are small (e.g., kv_pack, kv_shuffle) and do not saturate SMs — when they are launched in bursts they cause scheduler thrashing and increase overall kernel launch overhead.
3) CUDA graph amplification: We use CUDA graphs for the decode hot path. Prefetching causes graph re-instantiation for different KV shapes; graphs end up with many no-op nodes or small memcpy nodes inlined, which leads to inefficient graph replays that align poor with SM pipelining.
4) L2/backpressure and NVLink effects: For multi-GPU nodes with NVLink used for kv replication, the prefetch path creates contention on L2 and NVLink channels during the large batched copies, which leads to delayed downstream kernels on peer GPUs. Prefetchless small transfers interleave and avoid large instantaneous L2 pressure.
5) Host CPU scheduling: The prefetch path creates spikes of CPU activity (memcpy, page warm) causing jitter in the process that enqueues kernel launches (we see jittered enqueue latencies in trace). Prefetchless spreads CPU work out.

Repro steps (quick):
1) Deploy same binary with env: PREFETCH_KV=1 (A) or PREFETCH_KV=0 (B).
2) Use loadgen config: 4 workers, think_time 1000ms, seq_len 180. Record telemetry: /metrics/runtime and /metrics/nsight.
3) Start Nsight capture with the following CLI flags:
   NSIGHT_CLI: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --output=SESSIONNAME
   Capture window: 30s after warmup (warmup 60s).
4) Export timeline to .rdc and open on local machine; zoom into kernel burst regions and inspect host/device transfer rows.

Important Nsight capture settings used (notes for repeatability):
- nsys v23.5 with options: --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --force-overwrite
- NVTX annotations active in runtime around prefetch start/end, kv fetch begin/end, and decode token loop; ensure NVTX not stripped.
- Graph replay markers: runtime emits NVTX before/after graph launch.

Root causes (synthesis):
- Bulk prefetched copies reduce per-transfer overhead but move costs earlier in timeline, producing downstream bursts of small kernels that are expensive relative to their compute and poorly overlapped. The bursts reduce effective occupancy by creating short idle windows between bursts where SMs are waiting on kernel enqueue or slow L2 flushes.
- Streaming and priority interactions: prefetch uses same default stream for copy completion callbacks; those callbacks enqueue low-latency kernels on default stream causing priority inversion with decode kernels on a dedicated high-priority stream.
- CUDA graph interactions: graph structure assumes steady-state kernel sizes; introducing large copy nodes or variable-length copy nodes into graphs reduces effectiveness and increases replay latency due to reordering and side effects on scheduling.

Quick experiments tried (results):
- Move prefetch completion callback to a low-priority non-blocking stream: reduced kernel bursts (launchs/sec) by ~25% and tail 99 dropped from 58ms to ~41ms.
- Batch small prefetched kernels into a single fused kernel in runtime: gave a modest occupancy increase (~+6%) and reduced launch overhead; requires kernel-fusion work in opt-kernel-set.
- Switch to prefetchless with aggressive host->device async copy overlap (pinned pages, cudaMemcpyAsync in small chunks): this is current best balance for tail latency on mixed request patterns.

Actionable next steps (short):
- Short (1 sprint): implement stream rebind for prefetch completion (use dedicated low-prio stream) + test across NVLink nodes.
- Mid (2–3 sprints): prototype microkernel fusion for kv_pack/kv_shuffle in opt-kernel-set and run new Nsight sessions.
- Long: adaptively choose prefetch strategy per-request based on request size and inferred co-location (if multiple workers likely to touch same KV keys, prefetch improves throughput; otherwise prefer prefetchless).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to quantify memory pressure tradeoffs on smaller GPU SKUs (H100-80GB, RTX-class). Current tests on A100-80GB may mask fragmentation effects.
- Are there scheduler-level knobs we can expose (CUDA stream priorities, occupancy hints) to let runtime tune behavior per-model?
- How much does kernel launch API choice matter (cudaLaunchKernel vs graph-based replay vs persistent kernel)? Quick test suggests persistent kernel gives best tail smoothing but requires larger engineering investment.

Raw snippets and commands used:
- Run harness: ./tools/infer_loadgen --model chat-xxl --workers=4 --think_time=1000 --prefetch_kv=$PREFETCH_KV
- Nsight capture: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/session_prefetch_A nsys_capture_cmd --duration=30s
- Quick log grep: grep -n "KV_PREFETCH" runtime.log | tail -n 50

Notes to self:
- When presenting, include two side-by-side timeline screenshots (burst region vs steady region). Annotate NVTX for prefetch start/end, graph launch, and kernel queue intervals.
- Avoid claiming "prefetch is bad" — instead frame as workload-dependent: for steady high-concurrency workloads prefetch helps throughput, but for PLG-style spiky traffic prefetch can worsen tail latency unless we change scheduling/streaming.

Attachments (local):
- /artifacts/nsight/nsight_session_kv_prefetch_2029-09-15.rdc
- /artifacts/nsight/nsight_session_kv_on_demand_2029-09-16.rdc
- /artifacts/png/timeline_prefetch_burst_2029-09-15.png
- /artifacts/png/timeline_on_demand_2029-09-16.png

If helpful I can: run runs for H100 nodes, add persistent-kernel prototype, or post a short demo showing NVTX-annotated timeline with cursored metrics (SM active warps, achieved occupancy).

End of note.
